key_insight: The paper shows that nonlinear dynamics can be approximated for quantum simulation by learning a linear Koopman representation and executing its evolution with shallow quantum circuits.
engineering_relevance: This provides a near-term hardware path for simulating moderately nonlinear real-world systems on superconducting quantum processors beyond strictly unitary dynamics.
method: Learn Koopman observables from trajectory data to lift nonlinear states into a linear space.
Project the lifted dynamics onto a finite-dimensional subspace and convert the resulting propagator into spectral channels.
Implement the channelized evolution with parallel shallow quantum circuits on hardware.
evidence_signal: The approach was demonstrated on a superconducting processor across three systems—reaction-diffusion, spherical fluid motion, and Gulf Stream observations—using up to 32 parallel 10-qubit circuits.
watch_item: Accuracy is limited by both hardware noise and the finite-dimensional Koopman approximation, especially as nonlinear scale interactions become stronger.
paper_title: Quantum simulation of real-world nonlinear dynamics via Koopman method
